newsitem.title: CHINA: ING agrees real estate joint-venture.
newsitem.headline: ING agrees real estate joint-venture.

text.p: Dutch financial services group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) has signed an agreement to form a $24 million apartment construction joint venture in Beijing, senior company officials said on Tuesday.

ING Real Estate International would own 50 percent of the three-year venture to build about 600 residential and commercial units in the outskirts of the Chinese capital, ING Group executive board member Herman Huizinga told a news conference in Beijing.

CITIC Real Estate Co, part of the China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), and Beijing East Lake Real Estate Co would each hold 25 percent of the venture, ING CRE Urban Real Estate Co, Huizinga said.
ING was confident the apartments, which would cost $45,000 each, would sell well despite a weak market for high-class housing in the city, he said.
Construction of the apartments in Beijing's Wangjing New Town area was scheduled to begin in early 1997 and to take about two years, he said.
